draft.title: Finding sides in similar triangles
card: Similar triangles have the same shape but may be different sizes. Their matching sides are in the same ratio.
Matching sides sit opposite equal angles. Pair them up first, then compare.
To find the scale factor, divide a side on the new triangle by the matching side on the original. Scale factor = new length ÷ original length.
Worked example: Triangle ABC has sides 3, 4 and 5. A similar triangle has a side of 9 matching the 3. Scale factor = 9 ÷ 3 = 3. The side matching 4 is 4 × 3 = 12.
draft.remember: Find the scale factor from one matching pair, then multiply or divide by it.

a.q: Two similar triangles have matching sides of 6 cm and 15 cm. The smaller triangle has another side of 8 cm. How long is the matching side on the larger triangle?
a.why: The scale factor is 15 ÷ 6 = 2.5, so the matching side is 8 × 2.5 = 20 cm. Adding 9 to get 17 cm is tempting, but similar triangles are linked by multiplying, not adding.
a.clue: Find the scale factor from the pair you know, then use it.

b.q: Triangle PQR is similar to triangle XYZ. PQ = 12 cm matches XY = 8 cm. QR = 18 cm. How long is the matching side YZ?
b.why: Going from PQR to XYZ the scale factor is 8 ÷ 12 = 2/3, so YZ = 18 × 2/3 = 12 cm. Multiplying by 3/2 gives 27 cm, which is wrong because XYZ is the smaller triangle, so its sides must be shorter.
b.clue: Is XYZ larger or smaller than PQR?

check.summary: No problems found. Both answers check out (15 ÷ 6 = 2.5, so 8 × 2.5 = 20 cm; 8 ÷ 12 = 2/3, so 18 × 2/3 = 12 cm), and the explanations match the card.
